Predict risk from exactly the fitted model

Source: R/prediction.R
cp_predict.Rd

Checks the incoming rows against the schema recorded at fit time, then predicts on the response scale from the stored rms fit.

Usage

cp_predict(model, newdata, on_missing = c("stop", "na"))

Arguments

model

A cp_model().

newdata

Rows to score. Required: a model carries no copy of the cohort, both because the specification asks that patient-level originals not be retained and because a stored copy is one that can drift from the data the caller actually has.

on_missing

One of "stop" or "na". Rows with a missing predictor cannot be scored by a complete-data model; "stop" refuses them and "na" returns NA for those rows.

Value

A data frame with one row per input row: .pred on the probability scale, and .extrapolated marking rows outside the development range.

Details

The checks are the reason this is not a thin wrapper around stats::predict(). A factor level the model never saw cannot be scored, and rms signals that a long way from its cause, so an unseen level is refused here by name. A value outside the range the model was developed on can be scored, and is, but it is extrapolation and the result says so rather than looking like any other row.

easystats is not used for this. insight::get_predicted() returns NULL for an lrm fit, so there is no prediction path through that ecosystem. See inst/capability-matrix.md.

Examples

cohort <- cp_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
project <- cp_project("uds", "event", c("age", "bmi", "sex"),
                      cohort = cohort)
fit <- cp_model(project, cohort, nonlinear = "age")
head(cp_predict(fit, cohort[1:5, ]))
#>        .pred .extrapolated
#> 1 0.10013810         FALSE
#> 2 0.08130734         FALSE
#> 3 0.12202587         FALSE
#> 4 0.10521724         FALSE
#> 5 0.09260464         FALSE
